--- title: "[Schema]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} The column-lineage DAG: live columns plus archived removed columns. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/schema.py#L94-L544){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python Schema() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ``_live`` maps each current column name to its `ColumnNode`, in frame order. ``_history`` retains the nodes of columns that have been removed, so provenance can be traced *through* a dropped intermediate (e.g. a dummy column back to the categorical it replaced). Together they form the DAG; ``columns`` / ``dtypes`` and (later) ``summary()`` expose only the live view, while the provenance queries also consult history. Build the initial DAG with `from_frame`; the recipe then calls ``update()`` after each step to keep it in sync with the transformed frame. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The DAG is built by the recipe; read it back from ``FittedRecipe.schema``. Here a small pipeline imputes a missing value, rescales the numerics, and dummy-encodes a categorical — composed step by step with ``.add()``: ::: {#b8b35f54 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd from shoez import Recipe, StepImputeMean, StepNormalize, StepDummy from shoez import Selectors as s df = pd.DataFrame( { "age": [25, 41, 33, 52], "income": [50000.0, None, 62000.0, 88000.0], "city": ["NYC", "LA", "NYC", "SF"], } ) schema = ( Recipe() .add(StepImputeMean(s.numeric_predictors())) .add(StepNormalize(s.numeric_predictors())) .add(StepDummy(s.nominal_predictors())) .fit(df) .schema ) schema.summary() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
shape: (4, 5)

"age""float""predictor""original"false
"income""float""predictor""original"false
"city_NYC""int""predictor""dummy"false
"city_SF""int""predictor""dummy"false
``` ::: ::: ``age`` stayed in place through both numeric steps, so its ``source`` is still ``"original"`` — but ``dtype_history`` records the int → float cast that ``StepNormalize`` applied: ::: {#9fe9680d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} schema["age"].source, schema["age"].dtype_history ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ('original', [Int64, Float64]) ``` ::: ::: ``city`` was expanded into indicators and dropped. ``columns_from_source`` grabs everything a step produced; ``ancestors`` traces an indicator back through the now-removed ``city`` column: ::: {#7a7ad66f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} schema.columns_from_source("dummy") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['city_NYC', 'city_SF'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#d1380416 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} schema.ancestors("city_NYC") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {'city'} ``` ::: :::
